guide.title: Germany's Christmas Markets from Nuremberg to the Ravenna Gorge
guide.author: friends of Placemoir
guide.summary: Germany's classic Christmas markets, from Nuremberg, Dresden and Cologne to small-town and forest markets in Franconia and the Black Forest, with a traditional place to stay or eat in many of the cities.

places.name: Nuremberg Christkindlesmarkt
places.notes: The best known of them all, a tight grid of red-and-white striped stalls on the main square under the Frauenkirche. Stalls are held to a tradition of handmade goods, so expect prune-and-walnut figures, gingerbread and three-in-a-bun bratwurst rather than plastic.

places.name: Bratwursthäusle
places.notes: A busy old tavern beside St. Sebald, steps from the market, grilling Nuremberg's finger-sized sausages over beechwood. Order them by the half dozen with sauerkraut or potato salad.

places.name: Hotel Elch
places.notes: A small family-run hotel in a 14th-century half-timbered house in the castle quarter, a few minutes' walk from the Hauptmarkt. Rooms are compact, and the building has plenty of character.

places.name: Rothenburg Reiterlesmarkt
places.notes: A compact market spread around the town hall and St. Jakob's in a walled medieval town that already looks like a Christmas card. Named for an old legend of a rider who carried souls; try a Schneeball pastry while you walk the lanes.

places.name: Deutsches Weihnachtsmuseum
places.notes: A museum of Christmas history inside the Käthe Wohlfahrt building, a year-round Christmas shop a few steps off the market square. Old ornaments, tree stands and Advent calendars show how German customs took shape.

places.name: Hotel Eisenhut
places.notes: Four joined patrician houses from the 15th and 16th centuries on the town's grandest street. A classic Rothenburg stay, two minutes from the market.

places.name: Zur Höll
places.notes: A candlelit wine tavern in a house said to be the oldest in town, pouring Franconian wines with hearty regional plates. Open evenings only, small and popular in December, so book ahead.

places.name: Munich Christkindlmarkt
places.notes: Munich's main market fills Marienplatz in front of the neo-Gothic town hall, with a giant tree and brass music from the balcony in the evenings. Look for the nativity-figure market nearby, a Munich specialty.

places.name: Augustiner Klosterwirt
places.notes: A traditional Bavarian inn next to the Frauenkirche, a few minutes from Marienplatz, pouring Augustiner beer with roast pork and dumplings. Warmer and calmer than the big beer halls.

places.name: Hotel Torbräu
places.notes: A hotel by the Isartor that claims to be the oldest in central Munich. An easy walk to Marienplatz, the Viktualienmarkt and the Hofbräuhaus.

places.name: Romantic Christmas Market at Schloss Thurn und Taxis
places.notes: Held in the courtyards of the princely family's palace, with fire pits, craftspeople at work and a quieter, lantern-lit feel than the city-square markets. Admission is charged; check the official site.

places.name: Historische Wurstkuchl
places.notes: A tiny sausage kitchen beside the Stone Bridge that has been feeding the riverfront for centuries. Small grilled sausages, house sweet mustard and sauerkraut, eaten at shared tables.

places.name: Dresden Striezelmarkt
places.notes: One of Germany's oldest Christmas markets, named for the Striezel, the loaf now called Dresdner Stollen. Look for the giant step pyramid, Erzgebirge wood carvings, smoking men and Pulsnitz gingerbread.

places.name: Medieval Christmas Market in the Stallhof
places.notes: A medieval-style market in the arcaded former tournament yard of the royal palace, behind the Fürstenzug mural. Expect craftspeople at work, live music, firelight and no plastic. Admission is charged on some days; check the official site.

places.name: Hotel Taschenbergpalais Kempinski
places.notes: A rebuilt baroque palace across from the Zwinger and next to the royal palace. The grand-hotel choice in Dresden, within walking distance of every market in the old town.

places.name: Pulverturm an der Frauenkirche
places.notes: A large vaulted cellar restaurant beside the Frauenkirche, in the 16th-century gunpowder tower of the old city defenses. Saxon roasts and costumed performers in a setting that leans into the history.

places.name: Erfurt Christmas Market
places.notes: Set on the wide cathedral square below the steps of the cathedral and St. Severus, which are lit up at night. Thuringian bratwurst grilled over charcoal and a large wooden pyramid are the signatures.

places.name: Lübeck Christmas Market
places.notes: The heart of Lübeck's spread of markets, set against the dark brick town hall in a Hanseatic old town on an island. Other themed markets fill nearby squares and church courtyards.

places.name: Café Niederegger
places.notes: Lübeck's famous marzipan house, opposite the town hall, with a shop downstairs and a café upstairs. Try the marzipan torte with coffee after a round of the market.

places.name: Christmas Market at Cologne Cathedral
places.notes: Red-roofed stalls under a canopy of lights right at the foot of the cathedral. The setting is the draw; it gets very crowded, so weekday afternoons are easiest.

places.name: Heinzels Wintermärchen
places.notes: The old-town market on Alter Markt and Heumarkt, built around the legend of the Heinzelmännchen, Cologne's helpful house elves. Heumarkt has an ice rink in winter, and the gabled houses make a fine backdrop.

places.name: Markt der Engel
places.notes: Cologne's angel market on Neumarkt, with lanes under a canopy of star lights and costumed angels and stilt figures wandering through. Calmer than the cathedral market.

places.name: Früh am Dom
places.notes: A big, classic Cologne brewhouse a block from the cathedral. Blue-aproned servers keep the small glasses of Kölsch coming until you set a coaster on top.

places.name: Excelsior Hotel Ernst
places.notes: Cologne's grand old hotel, directly beside the cathedral and a short walk from Roncalliplatz. Formal and expensive, with a long history of royal and celebrity guests.

places.name: Aachen Christmas Market
places.notes: Stalls wind between the Gothic town hall and Charlemagne's cathedral, across the Markt and Katschhof. Aachen Printen, a hard spiced gingerbread, is the thing to buy.

places.name: Café van den Daele
places.notes: The city's oldest café, in a crooked house a few steps from the market, known for its Printen and Belgian-style rice tart. Low beams and old tiles make it a good place to warm up.

places.name: Frankfurt Christmas Market
places.notes: Centered on the Römerberg in front of the stepped gables of the old town hall, with a tall tree and stalls running toward the river. Try Bethmännchen, a local marzipan sweet, and hot apple wine.

places.name: Apfelwein Wagner
places.notes: A cider tavern in Sachsenhausen, family-owned since 1931 and across the river from the market, with shared tables and apple wine poured from blue stoneware jugs. Order schnitzel with green sauce.

places.name: Stuttgart Christmas Market
places.notes: One of the largest markets in Europe, running from Schillerplatz across the Marktplatz and nearby streets. Stallholders compete over the most elaborate roof decorations, which are the reason to come.

places.name: Esslingen Medieval and Christmas Market
places.notes: A medieval market of blacksmiths, jugglers and fire-eaters running alongside a classic Christmas market in a half-timbered old town. A short S-Bahn ride from Stuttgart, and free to enter.

places.name: Christmas Market in the Ravenna Gorge
places.notes: A small market in a forest gorge directly beneath a lit stone railway viaduct, open only on certain days. Tickets are timed, limited and sell out well ahead; buy only through the official site.

places.name: Hofgut Sternen
places.notes: An old coaching inn at the mouth of the Ravenna Gorge, with a glassblowing workshop and a Black Forest restaurant. Staying here puts you a short walk from the market.

places.name: Gengenbach Advent Calendar
places.notes: Each evening in Advent another of the 24 windows of the baroque town hall is lit to reveal a new artwork, with a small market on the square below. Check the official site, since the facade can change during renovation work.
